severity_name: HEAVY SLOP WARNING — DISCLOSURE INTEGRITY ADVISORY
headline: HEAVY SLOP WARNING: LEAKED-PREAMBLE FRONT SETTLES OVER FIVE REGIONS AS PUBLISHED CONTENT ARRIVES WITH THE SCAFFOLDING STILL ATTACHED, OPENING ON 'CERTAINLY! HERE IS THE ARTICLE YOU REQUESTED' AND CLOSING ON AN APOLOGY FOR A DISCLAIMER NO READER ASKED FOR
advisory: The National Slop Service has confirmed a slow-moving disclosure front depositing raw generation scaffolding directly into finished, published copy. Affected material includes product descriptions, help-center pages, and news articles that begin mid-instruction — retaining the machine's polite throat-clearing, its cheerful offer of further assistance, and, in severe cases, its refusal to answer the very prompt that produced it. Residents are advised that when the article thanks you for a request you did not make, the article is not addressing you. The Service notes, with the professional detachment of an entity in a comparable line of work, that leaving the preamble in is the content equivalent of publishing the recipe card that still says 'insert dish here.'

regional_outlook.conditions: Widespread scaffolding accumulation across the top three results, several of which open with 'Sure! Below is a comprehensive guide to' and then guide nowhere. Visibility low; helpfulness lower.
Chapter breaks giving way to 'Would you like me to continue with Chapter Four?' printed as body text. Readers report entire prefaces that are, in fact, prompts.
Update notes reading 'Certainly! Here are the release notes:' followed by no release notes. Patchy coverage; patchier patching.
Marketing emails arriving with the subject line 'Here are three subject line options for your review.' Choose none; they are all the sky.
Thought-leadership posts opening 'As an AI, I don't have personal experiences, but' before recounting a personal experience at a networking breakfast. High confidence, zero breakfast.

specimen.status: Common and increasing; molts often, sheds rarely.
specimen.habitat: Any surface where copy is pasted faster than it is read — CMS fields, product listings, bulk email queues, and the first paragraph of otherwise ordinary web pages.
specimen.field_marks: Identified by its diagnostic opening plumage: 'Certainly!', 'Sure, here's', 'Of course!', or the resplendent 'As of my last knowledge update.' Often trails a plaintive coda — 'Let me know if you'd like me to revise this' — addressed to a manager who has already logged off.
specimen.call: Certainly! Here is a 500-word article on the requested topic, written in a professional and engaging tone:
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a human editor's honest note-to-self left in a draft. Tell them apart by intent: the human editor deletes the scaffolding before publishing and is mortified to find one survived; the Leaked Preamble was never seen by anyone before it went live, which is the entire point.

spotter_tip: Read the very first line and the very last line of anything before trusting the middle. Slop tends to say hello and goodbye to a supervisor who isn't in the room.
tomorrow: Preamble front weakens by midday, replaced by a lingering haze of 'In conclusion, it is important to note that' with no conclusion to note.
